slides.text: Rust never turns one number type into another by itself. The `as` keyword does it, and it never fails: it always gives a value, even when the value changes.
Pseudo code, not Rust. `as` goes after the value and names the type you want.
slides.code:
value as target_type

7 as a wider type  -> same 7
300 as a smaller type -> may change

slides.text:
A cast keeps the bits of the value and fits them into the new type. A smaller type keeps only the low bits.

Pseudo code, not Rust. 300 in 16 bits, cut to 8:
A signed type reads the top bit as a sign, an unsigned type reads it as part of the number. The same bits can mean two different values.

exercises.title: Widen with as
exercises.guide: Turn a number into a wider type with `as`.

chunks.guide: Two numbers, then a wider copy of the first.

notes.text: as converts the number to the type after it.

chunks.text:
let small: i32 = 42;
    let wide = small as i64;

chunks.guide: A `u8` widened to a `u32`. The value stays the same, and adding after the cast cannot overflow.
Print the copies and the sum.

exercises.title: Fix the subtraction
exercises.guide: Rust never mixes number types by itself. Pick the fix that compiles and keeps an `i64`.
exercises.explanation: `as` is Rust's way to change a number's type. The other forms come from other languages and do not exist in Rust.

exercises.title: Narrow a number
exercises.guide: A cast to a smaller type keeps only the bits that fit.

chunks.guide: `300` does not fit in a `u8`, which stops at 255. The cast keeps the low 8 bits.

notes.text: No error: the value wraps around instead.

chunks.text:
let big: i32 = 300;
    let small = big as u8;

chunks.guide: `513` is 2 more than twice 256, so it wraps to a small number.
chunks.text:
let more: i32 = 513;
    let tiny = more as u8;

chunks.guide: Print the two results.

exercises.title: One byte of volume
exercises.guide: Cast `volume` to the one-byte type that makes the program print `232`.

exercises.title: Cut to 32 bits
exercises.explanation: `4294967297` is 2^32 + 1. An `i32` keeps only the low 32 bits, so what is left is 1.

exercises.title: Change the sign
exercises.guide: A cast between signed and unsigned keeps the bits and reads them again.

chunks.guide: `-1` is stored as all bits set. Read as unsigned, that is the largest number.

notes.text: Same bits, now read without a sign.

chunks.text:
let neg: i32 = -1;
    let as_unsigned = neg as u32;

chunks.guide: The other way: a `u8` with its top bit set becomes negative.
chunks.text:
let high: u8 = 200;
    let as_signed = high as i8;

chunks.guide: Narrowing and changing the sign in one cast keeps the low 8 bits.
Print the three results.

slides.text:
A float cast does not keep bits. Going to an integer cuts the fraction toward zero and stops at the smallest or biggest value the integer holds. `NaN` becomes 0.

Going from an integer to a float keeps the value, so small integers stay exact.

exercises.title: Integer to float
exercises.guide: Cast an integer to `f64` to mix it with a float.

chunks.guide: An integer count and a float price.
chunks.text:
let items: i32 = 7;
    let price: f64 = 2.5;

chunks.guide: `as` binds tighter than `*`, so only `items` is cast.

notes.text: Without the cast, i32 times f64 does not compile.

chunks.text: let total = items as f64 * price;

chunks.guide: Print the total.

exercises.title: Float to integer
exercises.guide: Casting a float to an integer cuts the fraction.

chunks.guide: A positive float cast to `i32` loses its decimals.

notes.text: The fraction is cut off, not rounded.

chunks.text:
let temp: f64 = 36.9;
    let whole = temp as i32;

chunks.guide: A negative float is cut toward zero, not down.
chunks.text:
let drop: f64 = -2.7;
    let toward_zero = drop as i32;

chunks.guide: Print both results.

exercises.title: A float too big
exercises.explanation: Unlike integer casts, a float cast never wraps. It stops at the biggest `i32`, 2147483647.

exercises.title: Cast before dividing
exercises.guide: Compare casting after a division with casting before it.

chunks.guide: Two integer counts.
chunks.text:
let hits: i32 = 3;
    let total: i32 = 4;

chunks.guide: Casting after the division is too late: the fraction is already gone.

notes.text: Integer division runs first, so 3 / 4 is 0.

chunks.guide: Cast both sides first. `as` binds tighter than `/`.

notes.text: Both sides are floats now, so the fraction stays.

chunks.text: let early = hits as f64 / total as f64;

chunks.guide: Print both ratios.

exercises.title: A pass rate
exercises.guide: Both counts are integers, and `9 / 12` would print `0`. Cast both operands to the float type so the program prints `0.75`.

exercises.title: A negative float
exercises.explanation: A float cast stops at the limits of the target. A `u8` cannot go below 0, so -5.0 becomes 0, not 251.

slides.text:
Only a `u8` can be cast to a `char`, because every byte is a valid char. A `char` cast to a number gives its code, and a `bool` gives 1 or 0.

Indexes and lengths are `usize`, so a number of another type is cast before it is used there.

exercises.title: Chars and numbers
exercises.guide: A `u8` becomes a `char`, and a `char` becomes a number.

chunks.guide: The number 65 is the code of a letter.

notes.text: Only a u8 can become a char with as.

chunks.text:
let code: u8 = 65;
    let letter = code as char;

chunks.guide: A char cast to a number gives its code.
chunks.text:
let initial = 'z';
    let position = initial as u32;

chunks.guide: Print both.

exercises.title: Shift a letter
exercises.guide: Move a letter forward by going through its number.

chunks.guide: How far to move.
Cast to a number, add, and cast back. The parentheses make the sum happen before the second cast.

notes.text: A char cannot be added, its number can.

chunks.text: let shifted = ('a' as u8 + offset) as char;

chunks.guide: Go backwards too: subtract the offset from the number of `'z'`.
chunks.text: let back = ('z' as u8 - offset) as char;

chunks.guide: Print both letters.

exercises.title: A score digit
exercises.guide: `score` is a `u8` holding 7. Build the character `'7'` from `'0'` plus the score, so the program prints `7`.

exercises.title: Booleans as numbers
exercises.guide: A `bool` cast to an integer is 1 or 0.

chunks.guide: Three flags.
Cast each flag to add them up. This counts the true ones.
Print the count.

exercises.title: Index with usize
exercises.guide: Indexes and lengths are `usize`. Cast to mix them with `i32`.

chunks.guide: An array and an `i32` position.
An index must be a `usize`, so cast the position.

notes.text: i32 cannot index an array, usize can.

chunks.guide: `len` gives a `usize`. Cast it to subtract an `i32`.
chunks.text: let left = scores.len() as i32 - pick;

chunks.guide: Print both.

exercises.title: Two casts in a row
exercises.explanation: 321 as `u8` keeps the low 8 bits, 321 - 256 = 65, and 65 as a `char` is the letter A.
